prompt: A force F acts on an object at an angle theta to its velocity v. State the formula for the power P developed by this force.

mark_scheme.criterion: States P = Fv cos theta (accept P = (F cos theta) v).

hints: Only the component of force in the direction of motion does work.
Include cos theta in the power expression.
solution: P = Fv cos theta (where theta is the angle between the force and the velocity vector).
teacher_walkthrough: Award B1 for P = Fv cos theta.
Emphasize that perpendicular forces (theta = 90 degrees) develop zero power because cos 90 = 0.

provenance.inspiration: Cambridge 9702 power with force at an angle
